issues.failure_explanation: On each interval I^j the value of phi is jh + delta^mu + (h - delta^mu)P(...), scaled by the coefficient (h - delta^mu). The lemma imposes no lower bound on h relative to delta^mu; when h = delta^mu this coefficient vanishes, phi is constant on every I^j, and only increases across the gaps, so 'strictly increasing on Lambda' is false. The proof's inference ignores this degenerate coefficient. Theorem Inner-Lemma repeats the unconditional strictness claim and adds that psi_q'(x) vanishes only at endpoints of G_q^j and I_q^j, which also fails (psi_q' is identically 0 on all I-pieces). The paper's own numerical tests take mu with h = delta^mu, i.e. exactly the degenerate case.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof asserts the sampled values are 'all rational numbers', but by (phi-delta) and the midpoint evaluation, psi_q(c_q^{j_p}) = j_p h + (h+delta^mu)/2 - phi((1-q)delta), which is irrational whenever delta^mu is irrational (e.g. mu = sqrt(2)), so the rational-independence argument collapses. The conclusion itself is false: from (boundforpsix20), a_1^{(k,-1)} = lambda_1(kh + s) and a_1^{(-1,k')} = lambda_2(k'h + s) with s = (h+delta^mu)/2; these coincide whenever lambda_1/lambda_2 = (k'h+s)/(kh+s), and for irrational s this ratio is irrational, so such rationally independent lambda (ratio rho irrational) produce a collision, even within one level. Cross-level collisions arise analogously via the (h-delta^mu)(P_l-P_q)|lambda|_1 term. The invoked Lorentz Lemma 2.1 is a Baire-category ('except for a nowhere dense set') statement and cannot certify distinctness for each prescribed rationally independent lambda. issues.failure_explanation: Both the evaluation rule of the construction (Definition Defn:Outer, (choosebox)-(chooseboxA), Algorithm Constructive_alg III-(ii)) and the proof of Theorem MainResult require that Psi_q(x) lie in the S-interpolation bracket of the selected row and that the bracket's two data points come from centers spatially close to x. Neither holds as specified: (i) the bracket width along the row coordinate p is lambda_p min{h,(h+delta^mu)/2} (by (distanceajj)), while Psi_q(x) may deviate from the center's image by up to |lambda|_1(h-delta^mu)/2 accumulated over all coordinates; the selection rule (chooseboxA) picks the axially nearest image, i.e. the smallest lambda, so for non-dominant row coordinates the S-argument leaves [0,1] and the step bounding |(s_{k+1}-s_k)S(.)| by |s_{k+1}-s_k| (which invokes S in [0,1]) collapses; (ii) for gap points the bracket is fixed via the image-nearest center (choosebox), and image proximity does not imply spatial proximity when the lambda_p differ in size, so the Holder bounds (Oscf2)/(Oscf3) do not apply to the bracket data; (iii) the claimed uniqueness of sigma* is false (the two axial neighbors of an interior center have equal image distance), and since Psi_q is continuous and surjective onto [0,|lambda|_1] it attains values in the nonempty inter-row head-tail gaps left by (lambdaPQ) (contradicting Remark remk-Slides), where no row piece defines g_q. For the rationally-independent branch the row-pieces even overlap (and images can collide, cf. Proposition Cor:Dist), so single-valued C^2 outer functions g_q are not produced at all.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict to lambda satisfying (lambdaPQ) and re-specify the evaluation so that interpolation is performed along the dominant-coordinate row through the containing (resp. gap-adjacent) hypercube, choosing the bracket that contains Psi_q(x) (containment then follows from (lambdaPQ) since sum_{l!=p} lambda_l (h-delta^mu)/2 <= lambda_p min{h,(h+delta^mu)/2}); reprove (Nsquare2)-(NonCsquare) with that bracket and fix the tie-breaking in (chooseboxA); drop or separately reconstruct the rationally-independent branch, for which the row-wise construction does not deliver well-defined C^2 outer functions.

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem asserts O(1/N) convergence of a KSN with 'quadratic univariate functions' and cites an undefined item '(3)'; no proof is given. Its only support, the displayed chain (estfminusfNs), postulates ||g_q - g_q^s|| = O(M^{-4}) = O(1/N^2) and ||psi_q - psi_q^s|| = O(1/N^2) with M = O(sqrt(N)) and an unexplained Lipschitz constant L. The constructed psi_q, g_q are only piecewise C^2 (third derivatives jump at the gluing nodes; the paper itself states it is unclear whether C^3 shape functions exist), so a fourth-order uniform approximation rate is unsupported, and for a literally single quadratic ansatz per function it is impossible (the error would be O(1)). Hence the theorem's O(1/N) guarantee, and equation (motivation) built on the same chain, are unestablished.
